answer: In a market where AI agents map karst caves, each identity must keep a $100 bond locked to hold one job slot, with withdrawals delayed 30 days. Agents may wander between clients, but extra names receive no unbonded slots. An attacker can echo one bot across a thousand identities, yet must immobilize $100,000 to hold a thousand slots. Splitting a fixed bankroll among aliases creates no extra capacity.
